title: Rotating-drum bidisperse granular segregation (Brazil-nut effect) verification surface
decision: Can a 2D soft-sphere DEM of a partially filled rotating drum reproduce (a) the literature Brazil-nut DIRECTION for at least 3 size ratios, (b) the segregation-degree SCALING magnitude within +-50% of the literature band, (c) at least 3 distinct segregation patterns including the axial banding mode, while all three required negative controls (ratio->1, omega->0, fill->1) drive the index to zero - or must drum segregation be declared WITHHELD as a verification surface?
prior_attempt_lessons: A concentration index alone is not falsifiable: bin-occupancy noise gives S ~ 0.06 for a perfectly mixed bed, so a 'monodisperse S<1e-6' criterion is only meaningful for an index that is structurally zero without a size contrast (size-position correlation). The prior attempt's vertical-vibration surface failed exactly this way (noise-dominated metric, |S| = 0.06 on the equal-size control).

A short time window (0.1-0.2 s of physical time, i.e. far less than one drum revolution) cannot produce segregation; the prior attempt's 'PASS' direction claims were therefore not supported by the data. This node uses >= 8 drum revolutions and reports the growth history S(rev).

Every segregation claim must be tested against a permutation null. The first design used a within-species position permutation, which is degenerate (the class position set is unchanged, zero null spread); this node permutes positions across all particles.
alternatives_considered: Continuum/analytic kinetic segregation model (rejected: no independent anchor, would not verify the DEM machinery)

3D DEM cylinder with axial bands (rejected for this node: cost, and no analytic anchor for the band wavelength; the axial mode is instead covered by a verified reduced-order Cahn-Hilliard banding model)
2D soft-sphere DEM drum + permutation-null statistics + reduced-order axial model (adopted)

operating_point_rule.rule: Reference point chosen from a physical criterion, not from the answer: the drum must be in the rolling regime, Fr = omega^2 R / g < 0.3 (cataracting threshold), with N >= 500 particles for percolation statistics.
operating_point_rule.value: R = 0.20 m, omega = 2.0 rad/s -> Fr = 0.082, N = 581 particles, fill = 0.30, d_s = 8 mm, d_l = 16 mm

hypotheses.H1: Coarse particles are enriched at the drum periphery (equivalently: fines form an inner core) for d_l/d_s in {1.2, 1.5, 2, 3}, significantly against the position-permutation null (|z| >= 3).
hypotheses.H2: The core-shell excess follows |excess| = A (d_l/d_s - 1)^alpha with alpha in the literature band 0.5-1.0 widened by 50% (0.25-1.50), R^2 >= 0.8, and a saturated amplitude at ratio 3 inside the literature order band 0.1-0.5 widened by 50% (0.05-0.75).
hypotheses.H3: At least 3 qualitatively different patterns appear: periphery (size driven), core (density driven, rho_l/rho_s = 3), mixed (controls), plus the axial banding mode of the reduced-order model.
hypotheses.H4: The monodisperse size-position correlation is identically zero (< 1e-6) and all three negative controls drive the index to zero.
hypotheses.H5: The reduced-order axial banding model reproduces its own analytic linear theory: growth rate sigma(k) = M k^2 (c - kappa k^2) within 3%, selected wavelength 2*pi*sqrt(2*kappa/c) within 10%, mass conservation <= 1e-10.

predeclared_thresholds.C1_direction: count(mode == periphery AND |z| >= 3) >= 3 over the 4 size ratios
predeclared_thresholds.C2_scaling: alpha in [0.25, 1.50] and R^2 >= 0.8 and |excess(ratio 3)| in [0.05, 0.75]
predeclared_thresholds.C5_negative_controls: (a) ratio->1 zero index + monotone growth 1.05/1.10/1.2; (b) omega = 0 mixed + amplitude monotone in omega over 0/0.5/1/2/3; (c) fill = 0.65 mixed + amplitude below the fill = 0.30 amplitude
predeclared_thresholds.significance: z from the position-permutation null (200 permutations), |z| >= 3

amendments_after_seeing_data.what: fill upper control point reduced from 0.75 to 0.65
amendments_after_seeing_data.why: at fill = 0.75 the random bed builder cannot place the particles without unphysical initial overlaps (RSA saturation at 0.55-0.60 area fraction). 0.65 is the densest preparable state and still strongly suppresses the free surface.

amendments_after_seeing_data.what: rolling friction coefficient mu_r raised from 0.02 to 0.10
amendments_after_seeing_data.why: with mu_r = 0.02 the spin DOF is under-dissipated and the static bed never comes to rest (residual rms speed ~0.09 m/s, a numerical 'boiling' state). mu_r = 0.10 is inside the usual DEM range for rough grains and brings the settle rms below 5e-3 m/s.

controlled: geometry (R, fill), contact law and parameters, particle size ratio at the reference point, time step, number of revolutions
confounders: particles are disks without out-of-plane porosity
limited number of revolutions (possible non-saturated state)
variables.repetition_rationale: The DEM is deterministic given the seed; reproducibility is checked with a second seed and the numerical sensitivity with dt/2 and n_bins doubled, instead of a seed ensemble (the permutation null supplies the statistical significance of each pattern).

outcome_metrics.corr: Pearson correlation of particle diameter with normalised radius (primary direction index; identically zero for a single size class)
outcome_metrics.S: area-weighted <|phi_L - phi_0|>/phi_0 over occupied radial bins
outcome_metrics.excess: phi_L(outer half) - phi_L(inner half) over the occupied radial range
outcome_metrics.z: z-score against the position-permutation null (200 permutations)
